doc.title: Ralph LaLama interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 23, 2010

title: Explaining improvisation to non-musicians
summary: Advice: listen more, start with Lester Young, learn it like a language, acquire a taste.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: If you had the circumstances to teach a jazz class, let’s say a non-musician jazz class, let’s suppose they were like almost senior citizens, and some of the people said “I just don’t get it, when the musicians just start going off, I don’t understand what they’re doing.” Is there a way to explain jazz improvisation to that kind of person.

Yes. I would tell them they would have to listen more. You know they would have to listen more, and maybe start off not listening to Coltrane. Start off listening to Lester Young. It’s just like learning a language. If you had a little kid crawling here he’d be going ma-maw-mama — you know he couldn’t speak it, even though we are speaking. He would catch it and catch it and catch it and then by the time he is sixteen he would say “hey Monk, buy me a car.” He knows how to speak that. Or she knows. Right? So it’s learning the language. You’ve have to get acclimated to it. And as far as liking it, you know I didn’t like broccoli when I was five years old or ten years old or fifteen years old. Now I eat broccoli every day. It grows on you, you know what I mean? And I know, that’s a good question, because I know just anybody, when I play I have a thousand people walk up to me and say, you know I never heard jazz before but I like this. You know what I mean? And I see it on people’s faces if they’ve never been to a place before or a concert, they look at you like you’re nuts, you know? Because maybe we were a little too strong for that moment for them. They should go back and listen and you know
listen to bla-bla-bla, you know? Sometimes you’ve got to acquire a taste or sometimes you don’t have time to acquire it, sometimes it hits you right away you just never knew it.
